rounds.text: Globus Spirits Ltd is trading at attractive relative valuation metrics compared to its sector, featuring a P/E of 25.68x against a sector benchmark of 29.37x [E6] and a striking EV/EBITDA of 10.34x compared to the sector benchmark of 55.7x [E11]. Profitability and capital efficiency metrics also shine relative to peers, with an ROA of 4.56% outperforming the sector benchmark of 2.63% [E8] and an ROCE of 11.07% besting the sector benchmark of 8.72% [E10]. Operational performance is underpinned by explosive recent growth, demonstrated by a TTM compounded profit growth of 283% [E21], robust cash conversion of 2.84x backed by Rs 270 Cr in operating cash flow [E34, E35], and expanding operating margins hitting 10% in TTM compared to 7% three years earlier [E30]. Furthermore, capital expenditure has largely completed with capital work-in-progress down 75.3% to Rs 37 Cr, signaling that new capacity is ready to come online [E40], while domestic institutions have aggressively increased their stake by 6.69 percentage points to 10.56% since September 2023 [E43]. Conceded: the stock has suffered a 12-month price return of -19.6% [E52], sits down near its 52-week range [E5], and features a discounted cash flow intrinsic value well below the current market price [E45].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 25.68x against a sector benchmark of 29.37x and an EV/EBITDA of 10.34x against 55.7x [E6, E11]. However, this relative multiple compression offers no comfort when a rigorous discounted cash flow model values the stock at just Rs 395 per share against a market price of Rs 893, yielding a severe overvaluation of -125.8% [E45, E46, E67]. Conceded: the ROA of 4.56% and ROCE of 11.07% outperform certain sector benchmarks [E8, E10], but these efficiency figures coexist with a depressed three-year median return on equity of just 7% and an overall low ROE of 8.41% [E9, E28]. The bull's reliance on short-term profit spikes like the TTM compounded profit growth of 283% ignores the longer-term structural decay shown by negative three-year and five-year compounded profit growth of -8% [E19, E20, E21]. Conceded: domestic institutions increased their stake to 10.56% [E43], yet overall institutional money flow registers as negative money flow with an institutional holding change of -0.43 percentage points alongside lagging relative strength of 16 [E44, E51, E69]. Finally, while the bull points to completed capital expenditures down 75.3% to Rs 37 Cr [E40], the rules-based screen scores the business at a lowly 43 out of 100 with a sell recommendation due to decelerating earnings and extreme valuation disconnects [E61, E66].
